alex: Quick write-up — ran a new set of load experiments to stress kernel selection + continuous batching under microbursty arrival patterns. Wanted to share observations and next steps.

sam: Nice — did you run both synth and capture-based traffic?

alex: Yep. Two harnesses: (1) synth: poisson+burst interp generator, (2) capture: 1h of real traffic replay with preserved inter-arrival deltas.

alex: Command for synth run: ```./harness --workload synth --burst-rate 3000 --burst-window 200ms --p50-iat 30ms --max-delay-ms 10 --batch-cap 64```

linh: Important that max-delay-ms was 10 — small delays usually favor kernel swaps.

alex: Exactly. Observed frequent kernel selector churn when avg seq len > 1024 and models flipped between fp16-kq and quant-kv path. Swap frequency ~2.4x vs steady traffic.

perf-bot: synth run summary: p50=18ms, p95=120ms, p99=380ms, avg-batch=5.8, kernel-swap-rate=0.42 swaps/sec/node

sam: Oof. How did the replay run compare?

alex: Replay was lower churn but worse KV cache cold miss tail. p50=22ms, p95=140ms, p99=540ms, avg-batch=6.2, kvcache-hit=0.87 overall but p99 miss spikes aligned with tenant bursts.

tasha: So synth had higher kernel swapping, replay had worse KV tail. That points at two orthogonal problems: kernel-selection heuristics being too eager, and kvcache eviction/spill patterns in multi-tenant mixes.

linh: Any visualization? timeline heatmaps?

alex: Uploaded quick timeline: kernel_id tracks, batch_size over time, kvcache_hitrate heatmap. Key pattern: when microbursts hit, batch_size briefly rises then drops — causing a swap to a low-overhead kernel which then loses perf on long sequences.

sam: Did you try forcing kernel pinning during the burst window? Like hold current kernel for X seconds after it’s chosen.

alex: Yes. Pin-for=250ms reduced swap-rate 3x, p99 improved ~18% on synth but on replay we saw degraded overall throughput for some long-sequence tenants (they were stuck on less optimal kernel).

linh: Tradeoff as expected. Maybe get decisive by tenant-weighted cost: prefer latency-sensitive tenants to avoid pinning to slower kernel.

alex: Another lever: increase batch-cap from 64 to 128 but clamp max-delay to 5ms. That lowers kernel swapping but raises queueing for high-concurrency tenants. Perf numbers: batch-cap128 max-delay5 -> synth p99 320ms, replay p99 510ms, avg-batch 9.1. Good for kernel stability, worse for fairness.

perf-bot: replay run (batch-cap128,max-delay5): p50=20ms, p95=130ms, p99=510ms, kvcache-hit=0.84, kernel-swap-rate=0.14 swaps/sec/node

tasha: We need a methodology decision: for apples-to-apples (normalized baseline) comparisons we should fix: same model version, same quant config, same sequence length distribution, and run both synth and replay with identical global QPS envelope. Otherwise differences conflate kernel vs input distribution.

sam: Agreed. Also recommend collecting per-tenant fairness metrics: p95 delta from tenant median, allocation of batch slots over sampling window, and KV miss attribution.

linh: For kvcache, I want to try prefetching KV for multi-turn sessions when session-affinity seen in 2+ recent requests. Prefetch cut cold miss spikes by ~30% in a small test.

alex: Test config: ```kvcache.prefetch=true; affinity.window=3; affinity.threshold=0.6``` — small test lowered p99 misses during replay bursts.

tasha: Action items: (1) alex: produce a short reproducible test spec for synth vs replay that enforces identical QPS envelopes and seq length histograms. (2) linh: run prefetch variant across three nodes and gather per-tenant fairness. (3) sam: prototype kernel-pin policy that is tenant-aware (priority + duration).

alex: I'll drop the spec into the perf board today and add the time-series + heatmaps link.

sam: Nice. One more ask — add a small config matrix we can iterate: batch-cap {32,64,128}, max-delay {3,5,10}, pin-for {0,100,250,500} and run short 15m runs. That should surface non-linear interactions.

perf-bot: queued jobs: 12 (matrix sweep). ETA ~2h.

tasha: Thanks — this is shaping a clear benchmark methodology. Keep notes concise so we can include them in the benchmark playbook. :thumbsup:
